mcqs.explanation: A test case is basically a documented set of activities that are carried out on the software in order to confirm its functionality to certain given inputs. Each test case would in turn have steps to address how we can check a particular test condition is satisfied or not.

mcqs.question: A type of testing that is conducted at the software interface.
mcqs.explanation: Black box testing is conducted at the software interface. White box testing is predicted on close examination of procedural details.

mcqs.question: A simple notation for the representation of control flow.
mcqs.explanation: The flow graph depicts logical control flow. Each circle in a flow graph is called a flow graph node, represents one or more procedural statements.

mcqs.question: A software metric that provides a quantitative measure of the logical complexity of a program.
mcqs.explanation: The number of regions of the flow graph corresponds to the cyclomatic complexity. All other options are invalid.

mcqs.question: An expression for the calculation of cyclomatic complexity.
mcqs.explanation: The option V(G) = E – N + 2 denotes the correct expression. Here, E is the number of flow graph edges.  N is the number of flow graph nodes.

mcqs.question: The probability of failure-free operation of a software application in a specified environment for a specified time.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is software reliability. It is estimated using historical and development data.

mcqs.question: SCM stands for __________
mcqs.explanation: Software configuration management (SCM), also called change management, is a set of activities designed to manage change by identifying the work products that are likely to change.

title: 13. Computer Fundamental MCQ on Operating Systems

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Multiprogramming”.

mcqs.question: A __________is a set of instructions which is prepared to perform a specific assignment if executed by a computer.
mcqs.explanation: A set of meaningful instructions is called a program. A program is basically designed to perform any function assigned to it.

mcqs.question: A program is an active entity.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is false. A program is not an active entity. It is completely passive.

mcqs.question: What is responsible for creating a process from a program?
mcqs.explanation: OS is responsible for creating a process from a program. OS stands for operating system. A process is created in order to be executed by using computer facilities.

mcqs.question: This cycle, of going through __________ states of running and input/output, may be repeated over and over until the job is completed.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is process states. The cycle of going through process states can be repeated over and over again until the job is completed or the process gets aborted.

mcqs.question: The wait fraction is represented by __________
mcqs.explanation: Wait fraction of a processor is represented by w. It is also known as the processor wait ratio.

mcqs.question: Processor wait ratio is given by ________
mcqs.explanation:
Processor wait ratio is represented by w. It is given by :
w=b/e+b.

mcqs.question: What does ‘b’ represent in a processor wait ratio?
mcqs.explanation: It represents the average I/O time. Average execution time with single programming is given by e.

mcqs.question: A technique that allows more than one program to be ready for execution and provides the ability to switch from one process to another.
mcqs.explanation: Multiprogramming is the concept implemented for execution and provides the ability to switch from one task to the other.

mcqs.question: Multiprogramming is mainly accomplished by:
mcqs.explanation: The OS is mainly responsible for multiprogramming. The hardware provides the specific circuitry that may be used by the operating system.

mcqs.question: The technique that increases the system’s productivity.
mcqs.explanation: Multiprogramming increases the productivity. By increasing the CPU utilization other devices’s utilization is also increased.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Multithreading”.

mcqs.question: Multithreading is also called as ____________
mcqs.explanation: Concurrency is often used in place of multithreading. Multitasking allows multiple threads to run at a time.

mcqs.question: Multiprocessing allows single processor to run several concurrent threads.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is false. Multitasking allows single processor to run several concurrent threads.

mcqs.question: A single sequential flow of control within a program is ________
mcqs.explanation: A thread is a sequential flow of control within a program. Single-threaded program can handle one task at any time.

mcqs.question: Both client and server release _________ connection after a page has been transferred.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is TCP. TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol. Servers receive requests from clients.

mcqs.question: Java extension used in threads?
mcqs.explanation: java.lang.Thread is the class that is extended if any user wants to extend threads.

mcqs.question: A method that must be overridden while extending threads.
mcqs.explanation: run()method must be overridden (It is similar to main method of sequential program).

mcqs.question: An interface that is implemented while using threads.
mcqs.explanation: java.lang.Runnable is correct. Any thread class implements runnable.

mcqs.question: A thread becomes non runnable when?

options.a: a) Its stop method is invoked
options.b: b) Its sleep method is invoked
options.c: c) Its finish method is invoked
options.d: d) Its init method is invoked

mcqs.answer: b) Its sleep method is invoked
mcqs.explanation:
A thread becomes Not Runnable when one of these events occurs:
• Its sleep method is invoked.
• The thread calls the wait method to wait for a specific condition to be satisfied.
• The thread is blocking on I/O.

mcqs.question: A method used to temporarily release time for other threads.
mcqs.explanation: We can use the yield() method to temporarily release time for other threads. It is static by default.

mcqs.question: A method used to force one thread to wait for another thread to finish.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is join(). We can use the join() method to force one thread to wait for another thread to finish.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Memory Management”.

mcqs.question: A task carried out by the OS and hardware to accommodate multiple processes in main memory.
mcqs.explanation: Memory management is carried out by the OS and hardware to accommodate multiple processes in main memory.

mcqs.question: An HTML file is a text file containing small markup tags.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language. It is a text file containing small markup tags.

mcqs.question: Secondary memory is the long term store for programs and data while main memory holds program and data currently in use. What kind of an organization is this?
mcqs.explanation: The secondary memory is the long term store for programs and data while main memory holds program and data currently in use. This is a physical organization.

mcqs.question: Memory organization in which users write programs in modules with different characteristics.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is Logical. To handle user programs properly, the operating system and the hardware should support a basic form of module to provide protection and sharing.

mcqs.question: An executing process must be loaded entirely in main memory. What kind of a memory organization is this?
mcqs.explanation: This is simple memory organisation. An executing process must be loaded entirely in main memory (if overlays are not used).

mcqs.question: FTP stands for?
mcqs.explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol. It is a type of internet service use for the transmission of files.

mcqs.question: A set of overlapping divisions in the main memory are called _______
mcqs.explanation: Partition main memory into a set of non overlapping regions called partitions. Partitions can be of equal or unequal sizes.

mcqs.question: Any program, no matter how small, occupies an entire partition.  This is called ____________
mcqs.explanation: It is called as internal fragmentation. Main memory use is inefficient.  Any program, no matter how small, occupies an entire partition.  This is called internal fragmentation.

mcqs.question: __________ is used to shift processes so they are contiguous and all free memory is in one block.
mcqs.explanation: Use compaction to shift processes so they are contiguous and all free memory is in one block.

mcqs.question: _______ searches for smallest block.  The fragment left behind is small as possible.
mcqs.explanation: Best fit searches for the smallest block. The fragment left behind is as small as possible.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Virtual Memory”.

mcqs.question: Separation of user logical memory and physical memory is ___________
mcqs.explanation: The separation of user logical memory and physical memory is called virtual memory. Only part of the program needs to be in memory for execution.

mcqs.question: Logical Address space can be larger than physical address space.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. Since, a part of the program needs to be in memory for the process of execution, the logical space can therefore be much larger than the physical address space.

mcqs.question: Virtual Memory can be implemented via __________
mcqs.explanation: Demand paging can implement virtual memory. Another way is demand segmentation.

mcqs.question: COW stands for?
mcqs.explanation: COW stands for Copy over write. COW allows both parent and child processes to share the same pages initially.

mcqs.question: LRU stands for?
mcqs.explanation: LRU stands for Least Recently used. LRU is least recently used. It replaces page with the smallest count.

mcqs.question: An allocation that uses a proportional allocation scheme using priorities rather than size.
mcqs.explanation: Priority allocation uses a proportional allocation scheme using priorities rather than size.

mcqs.question: A process selects a replacement frame from the set of all frames.
mcqs.explanation: Global replacement process selects a replacement frame from the set of all frames; one process can take a frame from another.

mcqs.question: Any program, no matter how small, occupies an entire partition.  This is called _____________
mcqs.explanation: It is called as internal fragmentation. Main memory use is inefficient.  Any program, no matter how small, occupies an entire partition.  This is called internal fragmentation.

mcqs.question: A process is busy swapping pages in and out.
mcqs.explanation: Thrashing is the term used whenever a process is busy swapping pages in and put.

mcqs.question: ____________ is one or more physically contiguous pages.
mcqs.explanation: Slab is one or more physically contiguous pages. Cache consists of one or more slabs.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “File Management”.

mcqs.question: A basic element of data in a file.
mcqs.explanation: Fields are the basic elements of data in a file. e.g. student’s last name. It contains a single value.

mcqs.question: Records are treated as a unit.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. Records are a collection of related fields. They are treated as a unit.

mcqs.question: __________________ refers to the logical structuring of records.
mcqs.explanation: File organisation refers to the logical structuring of records. It is determined bi the way in which files are accessed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an appropriate criterion for file organisation?
mcqs.explanation: The answer is Larger access time. The access time should be short. It is an important criteria for file organisation.

mcqs.question: ___________ itself is a file owned by the operating system
mcqs.explanation: Directory is the file owned by the operating system. File directory contains various important information.

mcqs.question: Which of the following isn’t a part of the file directory?
mcqs.explanation: File directory contains important information like: Attributes, Location and Ownership.

mcqs.question: Allocated size of a file comes under?
mcqs.explanation: Allocated size comes under the address information of a file. Address information consists of volume, starting address, size used and size allocated.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the usage information?
mcqs.explanation: Owner is a part of the access control information. Other options are a part of usage information of a file.

mcqs.question: When access is granted to append or update a file to more than one user, the OS or file management system must enforce discipline. This is _________
mcqs.explanation: When access is granted to append or update a file to more than one user, the OS or file management system must enforce discipline. It is referred as simultaneous access.

mcqs.question: The user can load and execute a program but cannot copy it. This process is?
mcqs.explanation: Execution is a process that user can load and execute a program but cannot copy it. Other processes are updation, changing protection, etc.

title: 14. Computer Fundamental MCQ on Application Software Packages & Business Data Processing

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Word Processing Package”.

mcqs.question: Category of software that comprises word processing, graphics, databases etc.
mcqs.explanation: Application software comprises of all these things like graphics, database, word processing softwares, etc. There are mainly two categories of softwares- System and application.

mcqs.question: There are two basic structures in text documents.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. There are two structures in text documents- logical and physical.

mcqs.question: MS-Word comes under __________
mcqs.explanation: Ms- Word is an application based software. It comes under document production. Ms-Word, frontPage, Frame maker come under this category.

mcqs.question: A ______________is an application that allows the user to compose and edit simple documents.
mcqs.explanation:
A word processor software is an application that allows the user to compose and edit all simple documents.
E.g. MS-Word.

mcqs.question: In text documents, a structure which stays the same no matter how the document is represented.
mcqs.explanation: There are two basic structures- logical and physical. A logical structure stays the same no matter how the document is represented.

mcqs.question: When the document gets put out : the best fit is calculated from ___________ structure.
mcqs.explanation: A logical structure stays the same no matter how the document is represented. The best fit is thus calculated from the logical structure.

mcqs.question: This can change the physical structure of the document.
mcqs.explanation: Formatting can change the physical structure. It includes indentation, text color, style, etc. of the document.

mcqs.question: An example of e-mail utility.
mcqs.explanation: Outlook is an example of email utility. Word is a word processor, Excel is a spreadsheet software.

mcqs.question: A structure that is system- dependent.
mcqs.explanation: The correct option is physical. The physical structure of a document is system-dependent; i.e., fonts and tab spacing vary among systems.

mcqs.question: The _____________ in a document and the order in which it is presented is referred to as the document’s logical structure.
mcqs.explanation: The information in a document and the order in which it is presented is referred to as the document’s logical structure. Information and the order are two most important things in a document.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Spreadsheet Package”.

mcqs.question: In a spreadsheet, letters are used to represent _____________
mcqs.explanation: In any spreadsheet, the letters are used to represent columns. The numbers are used to represent rows.

mcqs.question: Cells are identified by a combination of letters and numbers.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. A combination of the row number and column letter gives us the cell address.

mcqs.question: A numeric data analysis tool that allows us to create a computerized ledger.
mcqs.explanation: A spreadsheet package is the numeric data analysis tool. It is useful for any numerical analysis problem whose data can be organized as rows and columns.

mcqs.question: Which of the following isn’t a part of a spreadsheet?
mcqs.explanation: The answer is column number. There are no column numbers in a spreadsheet. Columns are represented using letters.

mcqs.question: Spreadsheets cannot:
mcqs.explanation: Spreadsheets are not meant to create graphics. They can do all sorts of calculations, plot charts and graphs, etc.

mcqs.question: ______________ help us to see patterns.
mcqs.explanation: Charts in spreadsheets give us a picture of our data. It can help us to see patterns as well.

mcqs.question: An easier way to set up complicated calculations.
mcqs.explanation: Functions make it easier to set up complicated calculations. Various formulae can also be used.

mcqs.question: The cell that is in use.
mcqs.explanation: It is called the active cell. The address of the active cell is shown in the formula bar.

mcqs.question: The placement of information within a cell at the left edge, right edge, or centered is :
mcqs.explanation: The correct option is Alignment. The left, right and center positioning is defined by the alignment.

mcqs.question: A change in the appearance of a value or label in a cell.
mcqs.explanation: Formatting is the term used whenever there are changes in the appearance of a value or label.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Graphics Package”.

mcqs.question: CAD stands for?
mcqs.explanation: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design. It is used in design of buildings, automobiles, aircrafts, etc.

mcqs.question: In CAD, objects are displayed in block format.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is false. In CAD, Objects are displayed in wire frame outline form.

mcqs.question: Used to produce illustrations for reports or for generation of slides.
mcqs.explanation: The presentation graphics are used to produce illustrations for reports or generation of slides for use with projectors Commonly used to summarize financial, statistical, mathematical, scientific, economic data for research reports, managerial reports & customer information bulletins.

mcqs.question: A graphics method in which one object is transformed into another.
mcqs.explanation: Morphing is a graphics method in which one object is transformed into another.

mcqs.question: Producing graphical representations for scientific, engineering, and medical data sets.
mcqs.explanation: Scientific visualization is the term used for doing the same. It is used in various science related fields.

mcqs.question: ________________applies techniques to modify or interpret existing pictures such as photographs and TV scans.
mcqs.explanation: Image processing is used in medical applications for picture enhancements, tomography, etc. It is also used to improve picture quality.

mcqs.question: A simple technique of X-ray photography. It allows cross-sectional views of physiological systems to be displayed.
mcqs.explanation: Tomography can be Computed X-Ray or position emission tomography. It allows cross-sectional views of physiological systems to be displayed.

mcqs.question: The major component of GUI.
mcqs.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface. The major component is the window manager. To make a particular window active, click in that window (using an interactive pointing device).

mcqs.question: GKS stands for?
mcqs.explanation: GKS-Graphics Kernel System is the first graphics package. It was accepted by ISO & ANSI.

mcqs.question: A set of libraries that provide programmatically access to some kind of graphics 2D functions.
mcqs.explanation: A set of libraries that provide programmatically access to some kind of graphics 2D functions comes under the graphics package. Their types are GKS, PHIGS, etc.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Personal Assistance Package”.

mcqs.question: A package that allows individuals to use personal computers for storing and retrieving their personal information.
mcqs.explanation: It is a personal assistance package that allows for the same. It helps in planning and managing their schedules, contacts, finances and inventory of important terms.

mcqs.question: PDAs have permanent rechargeable batteries.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. PDAs have permanent rechargeable batteries. They are standard alkaline batteries.

mcqs.question: PDA stands for?
mcqs.explanation: PDA stands for Personal digital assistants. They are generally hand held computers. They store, access and organize information.

mcqs.question: You can expand the memory of some PDAs with ________ that can be inserted into the PDA.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is storage cards. You can expand memory of some PDAs with small storage cards that can be inserted into the PDA.

mcqs.question: The devices that work the best with contact management.
mcqs.explanation: The palm pocket PC works best with contact management. The Palm Os is smaller, cheaper and have vastly better battery life.

mcqs.question: MCTI stands for Mobile community ________ inventory.
mcqs.explanation: MCTI stands for Mobile community tree inventory. It is a freeware tree inventory software. It uses palm OS and windows platforms.

mcqs.question: Forms that do not require any programming.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is hanDbase forms. The handBase forms do not require any programming. Pendragon forms can be used for a variety of applications like inventory for golf course.

mcqs.question: The forms that can be used for a variety of inventory applications.
mcqs.explanation: The pendragon forms can be used for the same. It can be used for a variety of applications like inventory for golf course, street, park, etc.

mcqs.question: Graphic object composed of patterns of lines, points, circles etc.
mcqs.explanation: A vector is a graphic object that can utilize various geometric shapes that can be represented using a few geometric parameters.

mcqs.question: Graphics composed of patterns of dots called pixels.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is Raster. Patterns of dots are called pixels. The raster graphics are generally designed in such a way.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “DBMS”.

mcqs.question: A collection of related data.
mcqs.explanation: Database is the collection of related data and its metadata organized in a structured format. It is designed for optimized information management.

mcqs.question: DBMS is software.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. DBMS stands for Database Management System. It enables easy creation and access of the database.

mcqs.question: DBMS manages the interaction between __________ and  database.
mcqs.explanation: DBMS manages the interaction between the end users and the database. End users are the final users that interact with the database.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not involved in DBMS?
mcqs.explanation: HTML isn’t involved in Database Management System. Other things like the data and application request are a part of the DBMS.

mcqs.question: Database is generally __________
mcqs.explanation: Database is user-centered. The perspective is that the user is always right. If there is a problem with the use of the system, the system is the problem, not the user.

mcqs.question: A characteristic of an entity.
mcqs.explanation: An attribute is a characteristic of an entity. The association among the entities is described by the relationship.

mcqs.question: The restrictions placed on the data.
mcqs.explanation: Constraint is a restriction that is placed on the data. Attribute is the characteristic and the relation describes the association.

mcqs.question: IMS stands for?
mcqs.explanation: IMS stands for Information Management System. It is developed to manage large amounts of data for complex projects.

mcqs.question: A model developed by Hammer and Mc Leod in 1981.
mcqs.explanation: SDM stands for Semantic Data Model. It models both data and their relationships in a single structure.

mcqs.question: Object=_________+relationships.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is entity. It is a part of OODBM (Object-Oriented Database Model). It maintains the advantages of ER-model but adds more features.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Components of DBMS”.

mcqs.question: DBMS is a set of __________ to access the data.
mcqs.explanation: Database is a set of programs designed to access the data. It contains information about a particular enterprise.

mcqs.question: DBMS provides a convenient and efficient environment.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. DBMS stands for Database Management System. It provides an efficient and easy to use environment.

mcqs.question: Which of the following isn’t a level of abstraction?
mcqs.explanation: There are three levels of abstraction: physical, logical and the view level. These three levels are involved in DBMS.

mcqs.question: A level that describes how a record is stored.
mcqs.explanation:
The answer is physical. The physical level describes how the record gets stored.
e.g. Customer.

mcqs.question: The ______level helps application programs hide the details of data types.
mcqs.explanation: The application programs hide details of datatypes. Views can also hide information for security purposes.

mcqs.question: A logical structure of the database.
mcqs.explanation: A schema is the logical structure of the database. e.g A  set of customers and accounts and their relationship.

mcqs.question: The actual content in the database at a particular point.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is Instance. Instance is the actual content of the database at a particular point of time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an object-based logical model?
mcqs.explanation: Network model is a part of record-based logical model and not object-based. Others are object based models. ER stands for Entity-relationship.

mcqs.question: SQL is _______
mcqs.explanation: SQL or structured query language is a relational model. It comes under record-based logical models.

mcqs.question: A level that describes data stored in a database and the relationships among the data.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is logical. The logical level describes the relationships between the data. Physical level describes how the data is stored.

title: 15. Computer Fundamental MCQ on Data Communications & Computer Networks

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Transmission Modes”.

mcqs.question: A term that defines the direction of flow of information between devices.
mcqs.explanation: The term transmission mode defines the direction of flow of information between two communication devices. It tells the direction of signal flow.

mcqs.question: Transmission mode controls the direction of signal flow.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. The term transmission mode defines the direction of flow of information between two communication devices. It tells the direction of signal flow between two devices.

mcqs.question: Which of the following isn’t a type of transmission mode?
mcqs.explanation: There are three modes of transmission: simplex, half duplex and full duplex. Transmission modes tell the direction of signal flow between two devices.

mcqs.question: A transmission that generally involves dedicated circuits.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is simplex. Simplex generally involves dedicated circuits. TV broadcasting is an example.

mcqs.question: A transmission mode that can transmit data in both the directions but transmits in only one direction at a time.
mcqs.explanation: The half duplex mode supports two way traffic but only in one direction at a time. The interactive transmission of data within a time sharing system may be best suited to half-duplex lines.

mcqs.question: A communication between a computer and a keyboard involves ____________ duplex transmission.
mcqs.explanation: It involves simplex duplex transmission. Another example of a simplex duplex transmission is loudspeaker system.

mcqs.question: Telephone networks operate in this mode.
mcqs.explanation: Telephone networks operate in full duplex mode. It can transmit data in both the directions.

mcqs.question: Fire alarms are based on this type of transmission:
mcqs.explanation: Analog transmission is a technique of transmitting voice, data, image, signal or video information. Fire alarm systems work in the same way.

mcqs.question: A technique of transmitting data or images or videos (information) using a continuous signal.
mcqs.explanation: Analog is a technique of transmitting data or images or videos (information) using a continuous signal, which varies in amplitude, phase or some other property.

mcqs.question: A walkie-talkie operates in ____________
mcqs.explanation: A walkie-talkie operates in half duplex mode. It can only send or receive a transmission at any given time.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Modulation Techniques”.

mcqs.question: A coaxial cable has a bandwidth of _________ of megahertz.
mcqs.explanation: A coaxial cable has a bandwidth of 100’s of Mhz. Baseband speed is in a few KHz. Multiplexing improves channel bandwidth utilization.

mcqs.question: In TDM, the samples occupy adjacent time slots.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. The TDM technique is based on sampling and they occupy adjacent slots and are transmitted in a sequence.

mcqs.question: The carrier wave is a _________
mcqs.explanation: The carrier wave is generally a sine wave. Carrier wave is used to transfer the signal from source to destination.

mcqs.question: Controlling the phase is referred as __________
mcqs.explanation: It is referred to as phase modulation. When there is a change in amplitude, it is referred to as amplitude modulation.

mcqs.question: A transmission mode that can transmit data in both the directions but transmits in only one direction at a time.
mcqs.explanation: The half duplex mode supports two way traffic but only in one direction at a time.

mcqs.question: A multiplexing technique based on sampling.
mcqs.explanation: TDM which stands for Time division multiplexing is based on sampling which is a modulation technique.

mcqs.question: An example of FDM:
mcqs.explanation: Broadcast radio is an example of FDM. This allows several messages to be translated from baseband.

mcqs.question: FDM stands for?
mcqs.explanation: FDM stands for Frequency Division Multiplexing. This allows several messages to be translated from baseband, where they are all in the same frequency.

mcqs.question: A modulation technique that improves channel bandwidth utilization.
mcqs.explanation: Multiplexing is a modulation technique that improves channel bandwidth utilization.

mcqs.question: The purpose of communication system is to transfer information from _______ to the destination.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is source. A communication system transfers information from source to the destination.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Multiplexing”.

mcqs.question: WDM stands for?
mcqs.explanation: It stands for Wavelength division multiplexing. It has same general architecture as FDM. FDM is frequency division multiplexing.

mcqs.question: In TDM, the samples occupy adjacent time slots.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. The TDM technique is based on sampling and they occupy adjacent slots and are transmitted in a sequence.

mcqs.question: In this type of multiplexing time slots are preassigned to sources and fixed.
mcqs.explanation: TDM is time division multiplexing. Data rate of medium exceeds data rate of digital signal to be transmitted.

mcqs.question: Controlling the frequency is referred as _________
mcqs.explanation: It is referred to as frequency modulation. When there is a change in frequency, it is referred to as frequency modulation.

mcqs.question: A technique that can be a solution to the problem of synchronizing data sources.
mcqs.explanation: Pulse stuffing is a technique that can be a solution to the problem of synchronizing data sources. In pulse stuffing, the outgoing data rate is higher than sum of incoming rates.

mcqs.question: For voice, each channel contains a ___ word of digitized data.
mcqs.explanation: In digital carrier systems, for voice each channel contains one word of digitized data. The data rate is 1.544 Mbps. Five out of six frames have 8 bit PCM samples.

mcqs.question: Many time slots are wasted in __________
mcqs.explanation: In Synchronous TDM, many time slots are wasted. Other techniques can help overcome this problem.

mcqs.question: A technique that allocates time slots dynamically.
mcqs.explanation: Statistical TDM assigns time slots dynamically. They are allocated based on demand. Multiplexer scans input lines and collects data until the frame is full.

mcqs.question: A system in which two channels are dedicated to transfer data.
mcqs.explanation: A cable modem has two dedicated channels from cable TV provider dedicated to data transfer. One in each direction.

mcqs.question: In this technique, there is a link between subscriber and network and a local loop.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Network Topologies”.

mcqs.question: A topology that is responsible for describing the geometric arrangement of components that make up the LAN.
mcqs.explanation: It is referred to as a physical LAN topology. LAN stands for Local Area Network.

mcqs.question: Bus is a type of topology.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. Bus topology is an arrangement where all nodes are interconnected using a single-cable.

mcqs.question: _____ LAN topology describes the possible connections between pairs of networked end-points that can communicate.
mcqs.explanation: A logical LAN topology describes the possible connections.  LAN stands for Local Area Network.

mcqs.question: A term that refers to the way in which the nodes of a network are linked together.
mcqs.explanation: Topology is a term that refers to the way in which the nodes are connected. There are 4 major topology networks.

mcqs.question: A network comprising o multiple topologies.
mcqs.explanation: A hybrid network consists of multiple topologies. It can comprise a ring, a star and other topologies. We call this arrangement as a hybrid network.

mcqs.question: The participating computers in a network are referred to as:
mcqs.explanation: They are referred to as the nodes. There are several topologies designed for arrangements of these nodes like bus, star, etc.

mcqs.question: A topology that involves Tokens.
mcqs.explanation: Ring topology involves sending and receiving of data with the help of tokens. Ring started out as a simple peer-to-peer LAN topology.

mcqs.question: A ____________WAN can be developed using leased private lines or any other transmission facility
mcqs.explanation: A peer-to-peer WAN topology is a relatively simple way of interconnecting a small number of sites. It has the least-cost solution for WANs that contain a small number of internetworked locations.

mcqs.question: A serially connected system of all the hubs of networks.
mcqs.explanation: The correct option is Daisy chain. This simple approach uses ports on existing hubs for interconnecting the hubs.

mcqs.question: A piece of information which is sent along with the data to the source computer.
mcqs.explanation: Token is the information that is sent to the source computer along with the data. This token is then passed to the next node.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Internetworking”.

mcqs.question: Configuration where many independent computer systems are connected.
mcqs.explanation: Distributed configuration has many systems connected, and messages, programs, etc are transmitted between cooperating computer systems.

mcqs.question: Partial mesh is a highly flexible topology that can take a variety of very different configurations.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. Partial mesh is a highly flexible topology that can take a variety of very different configurations. The routers are tightly coupled than the basic topologies. But they are not fully interconnected, as would be the case in a fully meshed network.

mcqs.question: Components used for interconnecting dissimilar networks that use different communication protocols.
mcqs.explanation: Gateways are used for this purpose. Gateways interconnect dissimilar networks, protocol conversion is performed by them.

mcqs.question: A  topology is a modified version of the basic star topology.
mcqs.explanation: A two-tiered topology is a modified version of the basic star topology. Rather than single concentrator routers, two or more routers are used.

mcqs.question: WANs that need to interconnect a very large number of sites.
mcqs.explanation: Wide Area Networks that need to interconnect a very large number of sites, or are built using smaller routers that can support only a few serial connections, may find the two-tiered architecture insufficiently scalable.

mcqs.question: Components that operate at the network layer of the OSI model.
mcqs.explanation: They are referred to as the routers. They are used for interconnecting those networks that use the same high-level protocols above network layer.

mcqs.question: A topology that involves Tokens.
mcqs.explanation: Ring topology involves sending and receiving of data with the help of tokens. Ring started out as a simple peer-to-peer LAN topology.

mcqs.question: ____________ operate at bottom two layers of the OSI model.
mcqs.explanation: Bridges operate at the bottom two layers of the OSI model. It connects networks that use the same communication protocols above data-link layer.

mcqs.question: Connecting two or more networks to form a single network is called :
mcqs.explanation: Connecting two or more networks to form a single network is called internetworking and the resultant network is called internetwork.

mcqs.question: OSI stands for?
mcqs.explanation: OSI is open system interconnection. It is a framework for defining standards for linking heterogeneous computers in a packet switched network.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “The History of Internet”.

options.b: b) Advanced Research Programmed Auto Network

mcqs.question: TCP stands for?

mcqs.question: The “Victorian internet” is actually?

mcqs.question: Packet switching was invented in?

mcqs.question: The probability of failure-free operation of a software application in a specified environment for a specified time.

mcqs.question: DARPA stands for?

options.b: b) Defense Advanced Research Product Agency

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “The Internet and its Services”.

mcqs.question: A network that links many different types of computers all over the world.
mcqs.explanation: Internet is a network of computers that links many different types of computers. It is a network of network sharing a common mechanism for addressing computers.

mcqs.question: Internet was evolved from the basic ideas of ARPANET.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. ARPANET is the first WAN i.e., Wide Area network that had only four sites in  1969 for interconnecting computers.

mcqs.question: A service that allows a user to log in into another computer somewhere on the Internet.
mcqs.explanation: Telnet is the answer. It is a service that enables the user to log into another computer somewhere on the Internet.

mcqs.question: An internet service that allows the user to move a file.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is FTP. FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol. It allows the user to move a file from one computer to another on the internet.

mcqs.question: Anonymous FTP files are called ___________ accessible files.
mcqs.explanation: Anonymous FTP files are called publicly accessible files because they can be accessed by any user on the Internet.

mcqs.question: TCP stands for?

mcqs.question: Any system that uses the HTTP protocol is called _________

mcqs.question: Any computer that can access the server is called?

mcqs.question: Allows the user to create and maintain a personal list of favorite URL addresses.

mcqs.question: URL stands for?

mcqs.question: The web works on this model.
mcqs.explanation: Web works on the client server model. Client and server operate on machines which are able to communicate through a network.

mcqs.question: In the Client-server model, the client receives a request from the server.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is false. The server receives a request from the client. It then performs the requested work.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a type of server?

mcqs.question: This determines the type of protocol to be used.

mcqs.question: Apache is a type of ________
mcqs.explanation: Apache is a type of web server. It is an application which waits for client requests, fetches requested documents from disk and transmits them to the client.

mcqs.question: A small data file in the browser.
mcqs.explanation: Cookie is a small data file in the browser. Most browsers nowadays allow the user to decide if they want the cookies or not.

mcqs.question: Any computer that can access the server is called?
mcqs.explanation: Any computer that has access to the web server is called the web client. Web server is any computer that uses the HTTP protocol.

mcqs.question: Allows the user to create and maintain a personal list of favorite URL addresses.
mcqs.explanation: Web Browsers help the user to maintain a personal favorite list of URLs. Also, allows the user to download information on various formats.

mcqs.question: SGML stands for?
mcqs.explanation: HTML(Hypertext Markup language) is based on SGML. SGML stands for Standard Generalized Markup Language.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “FTP & HTTP”.

mcqs.question: A program that can retrieve files from the world wide web and render text, images or sounds encoded in the files.
mcqs.explanation: A browser or a web browser is a program that can retrieve files from the world wide web. Certain examples are IE, Mozilla, etc.

mcqs.question: An HTML file is a text file containing small markup tags.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language. It is a text file containing small markup tags.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a type of browser?
mcqs.explanation: Others except web are web browsers. Web is a type of server.  Application that works on client requests.

mcqs.question: Both client and server release _________ connection after a page has been transferred.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is TCP. TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol. Servers receive requests from clients.

mcqs.question: In HTML, the tags that tell the browser how to display the page.
mcqs.explanation: Markup is a general term used to refer the types of tags in HTML. The markup tags tell the browser how to display the page.

mcqs.question: FTP stands for?
mcqs.explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol. It is a type of internet service use for the transmission of files.

mcqs.question: A section in HTML that contains generic information about the document.
mcqs.explanation: The head segment contains a generic info about the document. The head section must come before the body section in an HTML document.

mcqs.question: A tag similar to that of the italic tag.
mcqs.explanation: <cite> is a container tag in html that is citation generally in italics. Other tags like <em>or emphasize is also used for this purpose.

mcqs.question: A _________ partitions a web browser window so that multiple web documents can be displayed simultaneously.
mcqs.explanation: A frameset partitions a web browser window so that multiple web documents can be displayed simultaneously. Frameset can have attributes like cols.

mcqs.question: The _________ attribute specifies the web page to be placed in the frame initially.
mcqs.explanation: The src attribute or the source specifies the web page to be placed in the frame initially. It may be subsequently overwritten.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Abbreviations Related to Internet”.

mcqs.question: XML stands for?
mcqs.explanation: XML stands for Extensible Markup Language. It allows information to be shared among different computer systems on the Internet.

mcqs.question: AAA stands for Anonymous Administrative Authority.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is false. AAA stands for Autonomous Administrative Authority.

mcqs.question: API is?
mcqs.explanation: API is the application programming interface. It is a set of instructions that allow the creation of applications.

mcqs.question: GSM stands for?

options.b: b) Graphical System for Mobile Telecommunications
options.d: d) Global System for Mobile Telecommunications

mcqs.answer: d) Global System for Mobile Telecommunications
mcqs.explanation: The answer is Global System for Mobile Telecommunications. It uses a variation of multiple access on the basis of time and is widely used in Europe.

mcqs.question: IN stands for?

mcqs.question: FTP stands for?

mcqs.question: PDU stands for?

mcqs.question: A tag similar to that of the bold tag.

mcqs.question: ISP is?

mcqs.question: NE stands for __________ element.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Text Media”.

mcqs.question: ______________the ability to access, analyzes, evaluate and produce media.
mcqs.explanation: It is media literacy. It is the ability to access, analyze, evaluate and produce media. It is the process of becoming active, rather than passive, consumers of media.

mcqs.question: Media literacy can help youth and adults understand how media shapes our culture.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. Media literacy also develops our critical thinking. It also helps in the better understanding of how media shapes our culture.

mcqs.question: The analysis of _________ is a process of deconstruction that investigates the operations of texts, their constructions, the ways they produce meanings, what those meanings may be.
mcqs.explanation: The analysis of texts is a process of deconstruction that investigates the operations of texts, their constructions, the ways they produce meanings, what those meanings may be. However, they also warn of the dangers of making assumptions about the validity of any one analytic method.

mcqs.question: A type of analysis that attends to the repetition and frequency of features, their proportions within the text, and consequent assumptions about significance.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is Content. Linguistic analysis might concentrate on the potential effects of style of address. Content analysis attends to the repetition and frequency of features, their proportions within the text, and consequent assumptions about significance.

mcqs.question: __________ analysis regards texts as collections of signs or paradigms and possible meanings, operating within the bounds of various codes.
mcqs.explanation: Semiotic analysis regards texts as collections of signs or paradigms and possible meanings, operating within the bounds of various codes.

mcqs.question: This part of image analysis refers to those primary signs, often part of the technique of photography, which are about how the image is made.
mcqs.explanation: Treatment in image analysis refers to those primary signs, often part of the technique of photography, which is about how the image is made.

mcqs.question: In image analysis, this part refers to objects represented within the image, which may signify to us because of, for example, their symbolic power or because of their composition in relation to each other.
mcqs.explanation: Content refers to objects represented within the image. Treatment in image analysis refers to those primary signs, often part of the technique of photography, which are about how the image is made.

mcqs.question: _________ are about storytelling and story meaning.
mcqs.explanation: Narratives are about storytelling and story meaning.  Media texts tell stories; they have a narrative.

mcqs.question: __________ describes the effect of involving the reader with the story, of constructing it as truth.
mcqs.explanation: Identification describes the effect of involving the reader with the story, of constructing it as truth. It produces a meaning of truth, a belief in the validity of the text and of all the other meanings that we make from it.

mcqs.question: The notion of norms also links to the idea that representations are given force through a process of:
mcqs.explanation: The notion of norms also links to the idea that representations are given force through a process of naturalization.

mcqs.question: The  media texts may  throw up discourses and are called ____________
mcqs.explanation: Some texts may also throw up discourses and their meanings if you attend to what are called binary oppositions. The discourse is also marked by what it is not, by what it is opposed to.

mcqs.question: In terms of image analysis, it is important to attend to primary level signs in visual codes, most obviously for examples of still photography.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. This approach categorizes the image analysis into three: position, treatment and content.

mcqs.question: The notion of __________ is one which is especially associated with semiotics and with genres.
mcqs.explanation: The notion of codes is one which is especially associated with semiotics and with genres. The textual codes may be summarized into: written, spoken, non-verbal and visual.

mcqs.question: The idea of _________is central to understanding the production of meaning through texts.
mcqs.explanation: The idea of representation is central to understanding the production of meaning through texts. Texts are nothing but representations in both a material and an ideological sense.

mcqs.question: ICT stands for?
mcqs.explanation: ICT stands for Information, Communication and Technology. ICT is responsible for providing access to information.

mcqs.question: A system of interlinked documents, websites, portals etc. accessed through the Internet.
mcqs.explanation: World Wide Web a system of interlinked documents, websites, portals etc. accessed through the Internet. Since these links are not physical or mechanical, they are called `virtual’ links or `hyperlinks’.

mcqs.question: In image analysis, this part refers to objects represented within the image, which may signify to us because of, for example, their symbolic power or because of their composition in relation to each other.
mcqs.explanation: Content refers to objects represented within the image. Treatment in image analysis refers to those primary signs, often part of the technique of photography, which are about how the image is made.

mcqs.question: A dedicated website for providing specialized information in a particular field.
mcqs.explanation: Web directory is a dedicated website for providing specialized information in a particular field. Such directories are useful for educational purpose.

mcqs.question: _________ are the web-based interactive applications to express and share your ideas and thoughts with interested people.
mcqs.explanation: Blogs are the web-based interactive applications to express and share your ideas and thoughts with interested people. It is an open platform that can be used as on-line diaries, a journal, or editorial.

mcqs.question: A term used in the context of web design to suggest the path that user takes while browsing a website.
mcqs.explanation: Navigation is a term used in the context of web design to suggest the path that user takes while browsing a website.

links.context: This set of Computer Fundamentals Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Virtual Reality”.

mcqs.question: HMD stands for?
mcqs.explanation: It stands for Head Mounted Display. A kind of stereo display with two miniature screens and depth perception.

mcqs.question: In terms of image analysis, it is important to attend to primary level signs in visual codes, most obviously for examples of still photography.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. This approach categorizes the image analysis into three: position, treatment and content.

mcqs.question: ______________ keep track of position.
mcqs.explanation: Motion trackers keep track of position. Other devices are like head trackers and body trackers.

mcqs.question: BOOM stands for?
mcqs.explanation: BOOM stands for Binocular Omni-Orientation Monitor. It is a type of Stereoscopic display. Guidance of the box by the users.

mcqs.question: A term for Illusion of immersion by projecting stereo images on the walls and floor of a room.
mcqs.explanation: CAVE is the term. CAVE stands for Cave Automatic Virtual Environment.

mcqs.question: It is a mediated environment which creates the sensation in a user of being present in a (physical) surrounding.
mcqs.explanation: VR or virtual reality is a mediated environment which creates the sensation in a user of being present in a (physical) surrounding.

mcqs.question: A term to describe the extent to which a user can modify form and content of a mediated environment.
mcqs.explanation: Interactivity is the extent to which a user can modify form and content of a mediated environment. It comprises speed and mapping.

mcqs.question: A type of VR environment in which subjects are visually isolated from the real environment.
mcqs.explanation: In immersive VR, subjects are visually isolated from the real environment. A virtual scene is responding to the subjects actions.

mcqs.question: In this type of VR environment, the subjects can perform both in the real and virtual environment.

mcqs.question: ____________ is basically a form of pictorial presentation.
mcqs.explanation: Animation is basically a form of pictorial presentation. It has become the most prominent feature of technology-based learning environments.

mcqs.question: Multiplane camera was introduced by Walt Disney.
mcqs.explanation: The statement is true. Walt Disney along with his colleagues had a problem with creating realistic animation and how to conserve time while creating it. Therefore, they came up with a great solution which can be considered another innovation in the field of animation called the multiplane camera.

mcqs.question: It refers to simulated motion pictures showing movement of drawn objects.
mcqs.explanation: It refers to simulated motion pictures showing movement of drawn objects. Animation is a form of pictorial presentation.

mcqs.question: A ____________(invented by Paul Roget in 1828) is a simple mechanical toy which creates the illusion of movement.
mcqs.explanation: A thaumatrope (invented by Paul Roget in 1828) is a simple mechanical toy. It creates the illusion of movement. Thaumatrope means “wonder turner”.

mcqs.question: A device produces an illusion of movement from a rapid succession of static pictures.
mcqs.explanation: In 1843, William Horner, a British mathematician invented the zoetrope. A zoetrope produces an illusion of movement from a rapid succession of static pictures.

mcqs.question: The ____________ is a piece of equipment designed to make cartoons more realistic and enjoyable. It uses stacked panes of glass each with different elements of the animation.
mcqs.explanation: The multiplane camera is a motion-picture camera that was used in the traditional animation process that moves a number of pieces of artwork past the camera at various speeds and at various distances from one another.

mcqs.question: He made the first animated film in 1906.
mcqs.explanation: J. Stuart Blackton made the first animated film in 1906. Humorous Phases of Funny Faces was the first animation film.

mcqs.answer: a) Humorous Phases of Funny Faces
mcqs.explanation: Humorous Phases of Funny Faces was the first animation film made by  J. Stuart Blackton. He was using a blackboard as his workplace together with chalk and an eraser as his main tools.

mcqs.question: ___________ animation is used to animate things that are smaller than life size.
mcqs.explanation: Stop motion animation is used to animate things that are smaller than life size. Willis Harold O’Brian pioneered motion picture special effects, which were perfected in stop motion.

mcqs.question: The father of animation?
mcqs.explanation: J. Stuart Blackton made the first animated film in 1906. The film was entitled Humorous Phases of Funny Faces, and with this, he became known as the father of animation.

mcqs.question: Execution of several activities at the same time.

mcqs.question: Parallel processing has single execution flow.

mcqs.question: A term for simultaneous access to a resource, physical or logical.

mcqs.question: The measure of the “effort” needed to maintain efficiency while adding processors.

mcqs.question: The rate at which the problem size need to be increased to maintain efficiency.

mcqs.question: RMI stands for?

mcqs.question: A remote object is an object whose method can be invoked from another virtual environment.

mcqs.question: A typical _________ program creates some remote objects, makes references to these objects accessible, and waits for clients to invoke methods on these objects.
